results.title: resentation and then model item-item relationships through generative pretraining on large-scale, open-domain, recommendation-oriented item sequence data. Specifically, our work makes the following technical contributions: **1) Data Collection and Representation:** We compile a large-scale, open-domain recommendation dataset spanning 15 different domains (comprising 4.5M items and 35M interactions). We uniformly extract textual representations of items to serve as a data source for pretraining across various domains. **2) Unified Item Tokenizer:** Instead of relying on ID-based sequence modeling, which lacks semantics, or language-based modeling, which is often verbose, we propose a general item tokenizer that unifies item representations across domains. Each item is tokenized into multi-level concept IDs, learned in a coarse-to-fine manner inspired by curriculum learning. This hierarchical encoding facilitates semantic alignment, reduces vocabulary size, and enables effective knowledge transfer across diverse domains. **3) Autoregressive Pretraining:** We adopt an autoregressive modeling paradigm for pretraining, where the model predicts the next token in a sequence. This approach enables learning item co-relationships within a unified concept token space, thereby enhancing the model’s generalization in zero-shot and cross-domain settings. For clarity and consistency, we provide two pretrained versions of our foundation models: RecBase-0.3B and RecBase-1.5B.

item.text: {"text":"The closest 2024–2026 work supports combining shared content representations with collaborative signals, but the papers located do not establish effectiveness under the strict no-pretrained-language-model constraint. [CoCoRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.12183v1) encodes text attributes separately, quantizes them into shared semantic codes, and combines these with collaborative representations through cross-attention and masking objectives. It explicitly identifies the risk of textual features overwhelming behavioral relationships; its text encoder is pretrained. [FAME (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.12301) models multiple item facets with attention heads, experts, and contextual gating, but likewise uses a pretrained text encoder. [LLM2Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21579) reinforces the importance of interaction supervision for learning item relationships beyond textual semantics, while requiring an LLM.\n\nA feasible adaptation—not a demonstrated result from these papers—is a small, randomly initialized token or character-ngram encoder pooling titles and descriptions into a shared item component, added through a learned gate to an item-ID residual. Train all components jointly with the next-item objective so shared words receive collaborative supervision. Encode title and description separately; mask absent fields and fall back to the ID representation when both are missing. Compare against ID-only SASRec, text-only, title-only, and shuffled-text controls using the same macro validation HR@10. Examine sparse items and missing-text items separately. Textual overlap can suggest shared attributes, but compatibility, complementary purchasing, and current demand require behavioral evidence; neither these papers nor semantic similarity establishes gains on the specified four-category benchmark."}
